name: NCTF 135HA

lead: NCTF 135HA is a Filorga skin-booster solution containing hyaluronic acid together with other skin-supporting ingredients. It is injected into the skin in small amounts to improve hydration, radiance and fine wrinkles rather than to add volume.
The appearance payoff is fresher, smoother-looking skin on the face, neck and decolletage. Several randomised trials have examined it alone and combined with botulinum toxin or laser.

paras: A clinician places micro-injections into the skin over several sessions, usually spaced weeks apart. In trials it has been combined with moisturiser, botulinum toxin or picosecond laser treatments. Results in one study were assessed at 75 and 120 days.
In the multicentre trial most adverse events were mild. As with any injection, local reactions such as swelling or bruising can occur, and treatment should be done by trained clinicians.

chain: Hyaluronic acid cocktail injected into the skin
Fine lines look softer and skin looks fresher
angle.text: It is used to improve skin texture, glow and fine wrinkles on the face, neck and chest. Trials measured wrinkle reduction, hydration and radiance.

lead: NCTF 135HA is a bio-revitalising injectable from Filorga designed to compensate for skin dehydration, tiredness and fine wrinkles associated with ageing [1]. It combines hyaluronic acid with other components and is sometimes described as polyrevitalisation or a skin booster.

A randomised, active-controlled multicentre study of 146 subjects tested three sessions on crow's feet, neck and decolletage plus moisturiser against moisturiser alone [1]. Treated skin showed significantly reduced wrinkles and better radiance at day 75 and 120, hydration rose after treatment, and self-esteem scores improved [1].
Other trials tested it with other aesthetic treatments: with picosecond laser for melasma and premixed with botulinum toxin for facial rejuvenation [2][3].

paras: The main use is skin quality improvement: hydration, radiance and superficial wrinkles [1]. It has also been combined with botulinum toxin and with laser therapy [2][3].

A randomised, active-controlled multicentre trial of 146 participants assigned 3:1 to NCTF 135HA plus cream or cream alone found significant reductions in wrinkles in all three areas at day 75 and 120, with improved radiance, increased hydration, and mostly mild adverse events [1].

In a 2023 Moscow trial of 31 patients with melasma, 19 received picosecond laser plus NCTF 135HA and 12 laser alone; 89.5% of the combination group reported improvement versus 66.7%, and mean pigmentation reduction was 75% versus 40% [2].

A randomised double-blind split-face trial of 52 participants compared botulinum toxin A mixed with NCTF 135HA on one side against botulinum toxin alone on the other. Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale reduction was greater with the combination, and hydration rose only on that side [3].
